Stan Workflow: Factor Analysis with Sign Switching

Source: vignettes/stan-workflow.Rmd
stan-workflow.Rmd

Overview

This vignette walks through a complete example: simulating data from a one-factor model, fitting it in Stan with symmetric priors (which causes sign switching), and showing that DICi remains stable while the classic DIC fails.

To run this example yourself, copy the Stan model and R script to your working directory:

library(DICi)

# Copy example files to your working directory
dici_example("fa_marginal.stan")
dici_example("example_fa.R")

# Then run:
source("example_fa.R")

The Stan model

The key design choice is using the marginal likelihood. For a one-factor model, this means integrating out the latent factor analytically:

\[\mathbf{y}_j \mid \boldsymbol{\theta} \sim \mathcal{N}_P(\boldsymbol{\alpha},\; \boldsymbol{\lambda}\boldsymbol{\lambda}^\prime + \mathrm{diag}(\boldsymbol{\sigma}^2))\]

In Stan:

transformed parameters {
  matrix[P, P] V;
  V = tcrossprod(to_matrix(lambda, P, 1)) + diag_matrix(square(sigma));
}

model {
  alpha ~ normal(0, 5);
  lambda ~ normal(0, 1);   // symmetric: allows sign switching
  sigma ~ normal(0, 2);

  for (j in 1:N) {
    Y[j] ~ multi_normal(alpha, V);
  }
}

generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  for (j in 1:N) {
    log_lik[j] = multi_normal_lpdf(Y[j] | alpha, V);
  }
}

The generated quantities block outputs pointwise marginal log-likelihoods, which is what compute_dic_i() expects.

Simulate and fit 

library(cmdstanr)
library(DICi)

set.seed(2026)
N <- 400; P <- 6
lambda_true <- c(0.81, 0.72, 0.63, 0.54, 0.45, 0.36)
alpha_true  <- rep(0, P)
sigma_true  <- rep(sqrt(0.5), P)

eta <- rnorm(N)
Y <- matrix(NA, N, P)
for (j in 1:N) {
  Y[j, ] <- alpha_true + lambda_true * eta[j] + rnorm(P, 0, sigma_true)
}

mod <- cmdstan_model("fa_marginal.stan")
fit <- mod$sample(
  data = list(N = N, P = P, Y = Y),
  chains = 4, iter_warmup = 1000, iter_sampling = 1000,
  parallel_chains = 4, seed = 42
)

Compute DICi 

# One-liner with the cmdstanr wrapper
result <- dic_i_from_cmdstanr(fit)
print(result)
# Parameterization-Invariant DIC (DIC_i)
# --------------------------------------
#   DIC_i  = 5724.55
#   p_V    = 17.74
#   E[D]   = 5706.81
# --------------------------------------

Full comparison with all criteria 

library(loo)

log_lik <- fit$draws("log_lik", format = "draws_matrix")
log_lik <- unclass(log_lik)

# WAIC and LOO
waic_result <- waic(log_lik)
loo_result  <- loo(log_lik)

# Classic DIC: plug-in deviance at the posterior means of the parameters
# (averaging the pointwise log-likelihoods instead would give D_bar exactly)
alpha_bar  <- colMeans(fit$draws("alpha",  format = "draws_matrix"))
lambda_bar <- colMeans(fit$draws("lambda", format = "draws_matrix"))
sigma_bar  <- colMeans(fit$draws("sigma",  format = "draws_matrix"))
V_bar <- tcrossprod(lambda_bar) + diag(sigma_bar^2)
R_bar <- chol(V_bar)
Z_bar <- backsolve(R_bar, t(Y) - alpha_bar, transpose = TRUE)

D_bar    <- mean(-2 * rowSums(log_lik))
D_plugin <- N * P * log(2 * pi) + 2 * N * sum(log(diag(R_bar))) + sum(Z_bar^2)
p_DIC    <- D_bar - D_plugin

cat(sprintf("DIC_i:         %8.1f  (p_V    = %5.1f)\n", result$dic_i, result$p_v))
cat(sprintf("WAIC:          %8.1f  (p_WAIC = %5.1f)\n",
            waic_result$estimates["waic", "Estimate"],
            waic_result$estimates["p_waic", "Estimate"]))
cat(sprintf("LOO-CV:        %8.1f  (p_LOO  = %5.1f)\n",
            loo_result$estimates["looic", "Estimate"],
            loo_result$estimates["p_loo", "Estimate"]))
cat(sprintf("DIC (classic): p_DIC = %.1f\n", p_DIC))
# Output from a run with R 4.5.1 and CmdStan 2.37.0 (other versions or
# platforms can give different draws):
#   DIC_i = 5724.5, WAIC = 5725.0, LOO-CV = 5725.1
#   p_V = 17.7, p_WAIC = 18.0, p_LOO = 18.0 (true k = 18)
#   p_DIC = -217.7: negative because the chains switched sign

Applying to your own models

The workflow generalizes to any model where you can compute marginal log-likelihoods in Stan:

Model class How to get marginal log-lik
Factor analysis multi_normal_lpdf with \(\lambda\lambda^\prime + \Sigma\)
Linear mixed models multi_normal_lpdf with \(Z \Sigma Z^\prime + \sigma^2 I\)
Finite mixtures log_sum_exp over component densities
Growth mixture models Combine both: log_sum_exp over multi_normal_lpdf

For models estimated in JAGS or Mplus, see ?compute_dic_i.
